title: Language model identifies alcohol, drug and self-harm presentations in ED text
summary: Against a reference standard of 12.1% of attendances, coding identified 6.0%, clinician review 10.0% and a locally deployed large language model 15.6%, with the model's balanced accuracy matching or exceeding clinician review (n = 2,256 adjudicated). The model was applied to 105,096 annual attendances to estimate prevalence. It over-identifies and the study is single-site; this is a preprint.
ai_technology: Locally deployed open-source large language model classifying ED free text
organization: Centre for Cardiovascular Science, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK; UNSW School of Clinical Medicine, Sydney, Australia

evidence.tested: Diagnostic accuracy against a conflict-adjudicated reference standard.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other hospitals and the impact of over-identification; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A large language model classified free-text records to detect substance and self-harm involvement.
